\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Declared checks and implemented codes are matched by exact name. A renamed counterpart is a hand-assigned correspondence (counterpartMap in setup\_facts.py): the implementation covers a declared check under another name. Of the 6 codes without a counterpart, the four requirement-level licensing checks (\texttt{requirement\_*\_unlicensed}) were added on 2026-09-05 while the detectors were iterated on the development cases (C0 pilot). Cleared cases: risk cases that fail under C2 and not under C4 (denominator = each model's clearances). Strict counterfactual: only findings whose code is declared are kept, the frozen repairer re-repairs the frozen C2 artifact, and a case that still fails depends on undeclared checks; the lenient counterfactual counts renamed counterparts as declared. Neither simulates regeneration (cases still BLOCKed under the restricted validator, which would have triggered regeneration, strict: 0/0/0 in model order). The validator and detectors read no field of the contract file. Rule fixtures and mutation tests check selected behaviors without enforcing declaration--implementation equivalence.\par}
